items.title: Jaylen Brown ‘threw my phone across the room’ when he found out he was traded to 76ers
items.content:
Jaylen Brown revealed he was in sheer disbelief when he was traded to the 76ers. So much so that he chucked his phone.

The five-time All-Star was introduced to the Philadelphia media on Thursday and discussed how he found out he was being traded.

“When I first got traded I just threw my phone across the room,” Brown told reporters of his reaction to the July deal that sent him from Boston to Philly. 

“Who [reached out] first? It might have been [Tyrese] Maxxey. … He reached out and was like, ‘I know there’s a lot of stuff going on right now, but we [are] excited to have you.'”

Jaylen Brown of the Philadelphia 76ers talks to the media at Francis J. Myers Recreation Center on Thursday, August 6, 2026, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.  Getty ImagesBrown was acquired by the 76ers after much speculation about where he’d play in 2026-27. In return, the Celtics got Paul George, two first-round draft picks and two second-round draft picks.

Brown added that he’s still processing the news. He said the excitement of being in a new city with new expectations hasn’t worn off.

He also pointed out that he was in Boston for 10 years, over a third of the 29-year-old’s life to this point, and has to get used to his new normal.

A large part of his Celtics experience was shared with Jayson Tatum, and their relationship was rumored to have deteriorated throughout the past few seasons.

Brown, however, said Thursday that he leaves Tatum with nothing but respect.

Philadelphia 76ers guard Jaylen Brown poses for a photo during his introductory press conference. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect“We won a championship together,” Brown said. “Anybody that you win a championship with, you think that’s what a brotherhood or a lifelong legacy would entail.

“Obviously, there’s ups and downs in any type of relationship, for sure. On my end, there’s nothing but respect. Besides when he plays for the Sixers, I hope he does well.”

Another relationship brought into the limelight after the trade was Brown and 76ers star Joel Embiid.

Brown previously called out Embiid’s flopping on a livestream after the two had been cagey throughout the Celtics-Sixers first-round playoff series this past season.

Then, two weeks after the trade, it was reported that the two had not talked since the playoffs, leading Brown to clear the air.

“It’s been good,” Brown said about his relationship with Embiid. “Me and Joel been friends throughout the years, have mutual respect. I know he loves soccer, I love soccer, so we talk about that a lot.”

items.title: NBA star James Harden’s Houston gun case dismissed
items.content:
James Harden’s gun case will not linger into the NBA season.

The misdemeanor unlawful carrying of weapons charge that the Cleveland Cavaliers guard had been hit with stemming from his June arrest was dropped Thursday, according to court records viewed by The California Post.

The mugshot of NBA star James Harden released following his arrest. The Houston Police Dept.Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden’s gun case was dismissed in Houston today. Charles Wenzelberg / New York PostHarris County, Texas prosecutors wrote in a motion to dismiss the case that they were seeking to dispose of the matter after Harden had completed an “alternative resolution agreement.”

A judge formally signed off on the motion just before 4 p.m. CT, the records show.

Harden was taken into custody on June 13 by the Houston Police Department after he allegedly had an unholstered firearm in plain view in his vehicle during a routine traffic stop. AP Photo/Adam HungerMessages seeking comment from Harden’s attorney as well as the Harris County District Attorney’s Office were not returned.

Harden was taken into custody on June 13 by the Houston Police Department after the 11-time All-Star allegedly had an unholstered firearm in plain view in his vehicle during a routine traffic stop.

Harden never publicly commented on the arrest, though the Cavaliers said in a statement on the day of the incident that they were “aware” of the situation and were “in the process of gathering additional information.”

“We are in contact with James and his representation,” the team said, “and will continue to monitor developments as they become available. At this time, we will have no further comment.”

Harden spent nine seasons of his NBA career in Houston. He had played for the Los Angeles Clippers for over two years before joining Cleveland this past season.

items.title: Warriors Notes: Dunleavy, Offseason, Curry, Richard
items.content:
Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. hinted several weeks ago that the team might have a relatively quiet offseason, writes Monte Poole of NBC Sports Bay Area.

At a press conference in mid-May after head coach Steve Kerr decided to return to the team on a new two-year deal, Dunleavy said the team needed to find a way to reduce its careless turnovers and added that Golden State’s 37-45 record wasn’t due to a talent deficit.

“This isn’t about the roster frankly,” Dunleavy said. “This year, I don’t think we came up short because of the talent on the roster. It was injuries and things we can control. Do we need to get better roster-wise? I think so. But we didn’t get to a point where we played a team that the roster was better than ours.”

Dunleavy also said multiple times leading up to free agency that the Warriors were optimistic about retaining Draymond Green, Al Horford and Kristaps Porzingis. They not only brought back all three veterans, but re-signed De’Anthony Melton, Gary Payton II and Charles Bassey as well. The only new addition on the standard roster so far this offseason is No. 11 overall pick Yaxel Lendeborg.

Here’s more on the Warriors:

Despite speculation that the Warriors’ situation might frustrate Stephen Curry and cause him to request a trade at some point, Nick Friedell of The Athletic notes that the superstar guard has never publicly pressured the organization to make roster changes and it’s not as though the team hasn’t tried to make upgrades — the moves the club pursued just didn’t work out. A source tells Friedell that the front office has long kept Curry abreast of any players it’s interested in pursuing. The superstar guard has consistently expressed a desire to stay with the only NBA team he’s ever known, and Friedell doesn’t anticipate that stance changing.
In addition to focusing on cutting, converting open looks and playing high-level defense, second-year guard Will Richard also used Summer League as a way to improve his leadership skills, according to Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area. “This was a great opportunity for me to find my voice on the team,” Richard told reporters. “That’s not just talking and all that but leading by example. Making sure I’m coming here doing the right things and being a voice where the coaches can connect to the players.” Richard helped Golden State win the Summer League title in Las Vegas last month.
In case you missed it, Green recently discussed why he didn’t haggle over including an explicit or implicit no-trade clause in his one-year deal with Golden State.
